newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Paranagua ships 80,054 tns sugar to May 30.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Paranagua ships 80,054 tns sugar to May 30.

text.p: Sugar shipments are proceeding well out of the Brazilian port of Paranagua since the start of the crop year in May, with 80,054 tonnes exported to May 30, according to the port authority.
The port became the focus of attention last month when 260,000 long tons of raws ex-Paranagua were delivered against the New York May contract.
In addition to the Paranagua raws, the balance of a total of 339,950 long tons was made up from north Brazil and three Central American nations.
U.S. trade house Cargill was the receiver of all the sugar.

Under the New York contract, the sugar must be shipped by July 15 and given Paranagua's performance to-date, traders said there was now every reason to expect that all the sugar could be shipped in time.
Final figures for May are expected in the next few days but in the same month last year, the port shipped 23,182 tonnes of sugar and only 13,218 tonnes in May 1995.

The harvest in the center-south producing region traditionally only begins in May but even so traders say the supplier of the sugar to be shipped against the May contract maintains that it is using new crop sugar and not stocks.
In Brazil's main sugar shipping port - Santos - exports last month were very much down on last year, a port authority spokesman said.
Provisional figures for May were of only 6,549 tonnes of bagged sugar while the first bulk ship of the new crop year had only begun loading in the last few days, he added.
In May last year, the port handled 59,723 tonnes of bagged sugar, 27,819 tonnes of bulk and 6,675 tonnes at Cargill's private terminal.
Unica, the new body uniting virtually all the factories in the key state of Sao Paulo, is expected shortly to issue production statistics for the first half of May, a Unica spokeswoman said.

However traders said they had heard output was going well while a key producer said production so far was more or less in line with the same period last year when sugar output reached 362,155 tonnes by May 16.
